program.name: Federal Child and Dependent Care Credit (CDCC)
program.description_short: Federal tax credit for childcare or dependent care expenses when you work or look for work
program.description:
This is a federal tax credit for people who pay for childcare or dependent care so they can work or look for work. It can lower how much you owe on your federal taxes.

The amount depends on your income and your eligible care expenses. Lower-income households get a larger credit. This credit is non-refundable: it can bring your tax bill to zero, but you will not get any unused credit back as a refund.

If you are married and file a separate tax return from your spouse, you usually cannot claim this credit. Some people who live apart from their spouse may still qualify. A Dependent Care FSA through your employer will reduce the expenses used to calculate your credit.

This is a federal credit — there is no separate state application. You claim it on your federal tax return using Form 2441, and you will need your care provider's name, address, and tax ID number. Free filing help is available through IRS Free File and VITA sites; select "File Now" to start with IRS Free File.

navigators.description: AARP Foundation Tax-Aide provides free federal tax preparation help at sites across Missouri. Volunteers can help you claim the Child and Dependent Care Credit on your federal return. You don't have to be an AARP member. Visit the website to learn how to get tax help.
